record.original_question: What general theory of life can supply a mathematical definition of life together with general concepts and principles for living systems, rather than leaving biology with isolated descriptions that do not amount to a unified account of life as such?

evidence.quote: While the ultimate ambition of biology is a general theory of life, this remains an open problem: even general concepts and principles are absent [91].
Of primary concern here is the absence of a general theoretical definition of life and consequent realisation within an appropriate mathematical framework.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Formulate a general mathematical theory of life. Specifically: provide a rigorous mathematical definition of "life" (i.e., a precise mathematical predicate, structure, or class of objects within some specified ambient formalism—such as dynamical systems, stochastic processes, information-theoretic structures, category-theoretic objects, or other—that distinguishes living systems from non-living ones), together with a coherent collection of general concepts, axioms, and principles from which the qualitative and quantitative properties of living systems can be derived. The theory should be universal in the sense that it applies to all living systems (not tied to terrestrial biochemistry), and it should unify biological phenomena under a single account rather than leaving them as a collection of isolated descriptive models.
artifact.status_search_result: No accepted general mathematical theory or definition of life exists. Multiple frameworks (autopoiesis, (M,R)-systems, assembly theory, free-energy principle, autocatalytic-set theory) propose partial answers, but none has been generally accepted as supplying a unified mathematical definition with derivable principles. Recent surveys and the assembly-theory literature continue to treat the problem as open.

status_evidence.title: Assembly theory explains and quantifies selection and evolution
status_evidence.snippet: Assembly theory is proposed as a new framework, indicating the absence of a unified theory of life.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work proposes new frameworks because a general theory of life is still lacking.

status_evidence.title: What is life? — Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
status_evidence.snippet: There is no general agreement on a definition of life.
status_evidence.claim: No consensus mathematical or general definition of life exists.
